sections.skill: Protect accounts with unique passwords, two-step login and backups

questions.prompt: What does two-step login add?

choices.text: An automatic backup of every file
A longer username for the account
A second password that is the same as the first
A second proof, so a stolen password alone is not enough

questions.correct_answer: A second proof, so a stolen password alone is not enough
questions.intro: Business accounts (bank, email, website, payment processor) are valuable targets. Basics: use a long, UNIQUE password for each account, stored in a PASSWORD MANAGER (a secure app that remembers passwords). Turn on TWO-STEP LOGIN (also called two-factor authentication), which asks for a second proof, such as a code from an app, so a stolen password alone is not enough. Keep BACKUPS of important files in a separate place and test that you can restore them. Be wary of messages asking for codes or passwords.

sections.skill: A door lock plus a security guard

questions.prompt: A password is like what?
questions.correct_answer: A door key
questions.intro: A password is like a door key. If someone copies your key, they can walk in. Two-step login is like a guard who also checks your face: a copied key alone is not enough. Using the same key for your house, car and office means one lost key opens everything. A backup is a copy of your important papers kept somewhere else, in case of fire.
